proofs.proof_tex:
We give an explicit regular-submodel certificate and then derive the claimed rate-free obstruction from its fixed-error lower bound.  A procedure that is uniformly valid over \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}\) must in particular be valid on every admissible submodel constructed below.

Take one stratum \(\mathcal X=\{x\}\), take \(\mathcal Z=\mathcal A=\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), and let \(Z\) be uniform on \(\mathcal Z\).  If the support-restricted class is nonempty, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}stratum\text{-}instrument\text{-}support}\) implies \(K\pi_{\min}\leq1\), so this design has \(\pi_{xz}=1/K\geq\pi_{\min}>0\).  For every \(\tau\in(-1/8,1/8)\), define
\[
 m_0(\tau)=\tfrac12,\qquad
 m_1(\tau)=\tfrac12+\tau,\qquad
 m_a(\tau)=\tfrac14\quad(2\leq a<K).
\]
Conditional on the degenerate value \(X=x\), draw the binary coordinates \(Y(a)\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), independently with
\[
 \Pr\{Y(a)=1\mid X=x\}=m_a(\tau),
\]
independently of \(Z\).  Set \(A(z)=z\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\), and define \(A=A(Z)\) and \(Y=Y(A)\).  Independence of \(Z\) from the complete finite response type \(((A(z))_z,(Y(a))_a)\) verifies Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}instrument\text{-}randomization}\).  The two defining observation equations verify Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}exclusion}\).  The displayed joint distribution of the binary response vector induces a nonnegative vector of response-type probabilities summing to one, so it is a feasible member of every displayed response fiber and verifies Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}response\text{-}fiber\text{-}compatibility}\).  Thus the resulting observable law \(P_\tau\) belongs to \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}\).

The observable map sends this structural law to the law of \(O=(X,Z,A,Y)\) with conditional cells
\[
 p_{xzay}(\tau)
 =\mathbf 1\{a=z\}m_z(\tau)^y\{1-m_z(\tau)\}^{1-y}.
\]
The unobserved causal parameter in stratum \(x\) is
\[
 \theta_x=\bigl(E_\tau\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}\bigr)_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \in[0,1]^K.
\]
Under the maintained response-type restrictions, its identified set at the observable law is
\[
 \Theta_I(P_\tau)
 =\{Cw:w\in\mathcal W_x(p_x(\tau))\}
 =\mathcal M_x(p_x(\tau)),
\]
where the first equality is the response-type projection in Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}response\text{-}fiber}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}action\text{-}mean\text{-}polytope}\).  We next compute this identified set rather than stipulating it.

Let \(w\in\mathcal W_x(p_x(\tau))\).  Although Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}response\text{-}fiber}\) deletes one observed-cell equality for each \(z\), all deleted equalities are recovered: for any fixed \(z\), the model-implied probabilities across \((a,y)\) sum to \(\mathbf 1^\top w=1\), as do the observed cells, so the omitted equality is the difference between the two unit sums and the retained equalities.  Hence \(Bw=p_x(\tau)\).  Every observed cell with \(a\neq z\) has probability zero.  Nonnegativity of \(w\) therefore gives, for every response type \(r\),
\[
 w_r>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a_r(z)=z
 \quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal Z.
\]
Indeed, if \(a_r(z)\neq z\), the type contributes the strictly positive amount \(w_r\) to exactly one zero-probability off-diagonal cell at that \(z\), contradicting the corresponding equality in \(Bw=p_x(\tau)\).  For each \(a\in\mathcal A\), the equality for the observed cell \((Z,A,Y)=(a,a,1)\) now yields
\[
 (Cw)_a
 =\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r y_r(a)
 =P_\tau(Y=1\mid X=x,Z=a)
 =m_a(\tau).
\]
Thus every compatible response law has the same action-mean vector.  Conversely, the response-type distribution constructed above is feasible and has that vector.  Consequently the bound is sharp and singleton-valued:
\[
 \Theta_I(P_\tau)=\mathcal M_x(p_x(\tau))=\{m(\tau)\}.
\]
This proves the relationship between the causal parameter and the observed-law identifying functional.

We next use simplex extreme-point algebra to solve the decision problem.  For a singleton identified set, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}saddle}\) gives, for every \(q\in\Delta_K\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_x(q,p_x(\tau))
 &=\max_{b\in\mathcal A}(e_b-q)^\top m(\tau)\\
 &=\max_{b\in\mathcal A}m_b(\tau)-q^\top m(\tau).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first term is independent of \(q\), while \(q^\top m(\tau)\) is a convex combination of the coordinates of \(m(\tau)\).  It is maximized exactly by those \(q\) supported on the maximizing coordinates.  Since \(m_a(\tau)=1/4\) for \(a\geq2\), direct comparison of coordinates gives
\[
 Q_x^*(p_x(0))=\operatorname{conv}\{e_0,e_1\},
\]
\[
 Q_x^*(p_x(\tau))=\{e_1\}\quad(\tau>0),
 \qquad
 Q_x^*(p_x(\tau))=\{e_0\}\quad(\tau<0).
\]
Thus \(\tau=0\) is a codimension-one intersection of optimal faces, and perturbations of opposite signs select opposite endpoints.

Let \(\widehat S_n\) be an arbitrary data-based random closed set.  Give Hausdorff and support-function distances their extended value \(+\infty\) whenever the realized set is not nonempty and compact; such realizations cannot aid a contraction claim.  For a nonempty compact set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^K\), write \(h_S(u)=\sup_{s\in S}u^\top s\), and define the support-function distance as
\[
 d_{\mathrm{sf}}(S,T)
 =\sup_{\lVert u\rVert_2\leq1}|h_S(u)-h_T(u)|.
\]
Suppose \(\widehat S_n\) has asymptotic containment coverage at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly along all \(n^{-1/2}\)-local sequences through the preceding face intersection.  The constant sequence \(P_0\) is one such sequence, so honesty implies
\[
 P_0^n\!\left\{\operatorname{conv}\{e_0,e_1\}\subseteq\widehat S_n\right\}
 \geq1-\alpha-o(1).
\]

Fix \(c>0\) and set \(\tau_n=c/\sqrt n\).  Exactly two entries of \(p_x(\tau_n)-p_x(0)\) are nonzero, equal to \(\tau_n\) and \(-\tau_n\), so \((P_{\tau_n})_n\) is an \(n^{-1/2}\)-local sequence through \(P_0\); also \(|\tau_n|<1/8\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  With \(L_\tau=dP_\tau/dP_0\), direct division of cell probabilities gives
\[
 L_\tau=
 \begin{cases}
 1+2\tau,&(Z,A,Y)=(1,1,1),\\
 1-2\tau,&(Z,A,Y)=(1,1,0),\\
 1,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The two exceptional cells each have \(P_0\)-probability \(1/(2K)\).  Therefore
\[
 E_0(L_\tau-1)^2
 =\frac{1}{2K}(2\tau)^2+\frac{1}{2K}(-2\tau)^2
 =\frac{4\tau^2}{K}.
\]
Under Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}sampling}\), the product likelihood ratio is \(L_{\tau_n}^{(n)}=\prod_{i=1}^nL_{\tau_n}(O_i)\).  Since \(E_0L_{\tau_n}=1\), independence yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_0\!\left(L_{\tau_n}^{(n)}-1\right)^2
 &=E_0\!\left\{(L_{\tau_n}^{(n)})^2\right\}-1\\
 &=\left\{E_0(L_{\tau_n}^2)\right\}^n-1\\
 &=\left(1+\frac{4\tau_n^2}{K}\right)^n-1\\
 &\leq \exp(4c^2/K)-1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For any event \(E\), the likelihood-ratio identity and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |P_{\tau_n}^n(E)-P_0^n(E)|
 &\leq \frac12E_0|L_{\tau_n}^{(n)}-1|\\
 &\leq\frac12\left[E_0\!\left\{(L_{\tau_n}^{(n)}-1)^2\right\}\right]^{1/2}\\
 &\leq \rho_K(c):=\frac12\sqrt{\exp(4c^2/K)-1}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Because \(\rho_K(c)\to0\) as \(c\downarrow0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), choose \(c\) so that \(\rho_K(c)<1-\alpha\), and set
\[
 \delta=1-\alpha-\rho_K(c)>0.
\]
Transfer of the coverage event from \(P_0^n\) to \(P_{\tau_n}^n\) then gives
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\tau_n}^n\{e_0\in\widehat S_n\}
 \geq\delta>0.
\]

Under \(P_{\tau_n}\), the exact population optimizer correspondence is \(\{e_1\}\).  On the event \(e_0\in\widehat S_n\), the directed distance from \(\widehat S_n\) to \(\{e_1\}\) gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm H}(\widehat S_n,\{e_1\})
 \geq\lVert e_0-e_1\rVert_2=\sqrt2.
\]
For the support-function distance, take \(u=(e_0-e_1)/\sqrt2\).  Then \(\lVert u\rVert_2=1\), and on the same event
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_{\mathrm{sf}}(\widehat S_n,\{e_1\})
 &\geq h_{\widehat S_n}(u)-h_{\{e_1\}}(u)\\
 &\geq u^\top(e_0-e_1)=\sqrt2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Writing \(d_n\) for either distance, we have proved the fixed-error certificate
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\tau_n}^n\{d_n\geq\sqrt2\}\geq\delta>0.
\]

This fixed lower bound rules out every vanishing contraction rate, not only the root-\(n\) rate.  Indeed, let \((r_n)_n\) be any deterministic positive sequence with \(r_n\to0\), and fix any finite \(M>0\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(Mr_n<\sqrt2\), whence
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\tau_n}^n\{d_n/r_n>M\}
 \geq\delta>0.
\]
Thus \(d_n/r_n\) is not tight along this admissible local sequence, so uniform \(O_P(r_n)\) contraction is impossible for every vanishing \(r_n\).  Moreover, for every fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,\sqrt2)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\tau_n}^n\{d_n>\epsilon\}
 \geq\delta>0,
\]
which rules out uniform consistency itself.  Taking \(r_n=n^{-1/2}\) yields the advertised root-\(n\) impossibility as a special case.  The argument treated \(\widehat S_n\) as arbitrary, so it applies in particular to sets produced by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{face}}\), and no population face was selected.

Finally, this impossibility does not contradict exact confidence-set inversion.  The already-established Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}cp\text{-}correspondence\text{-}coverage}\) gives uniform finite-sample containment coverage for the confidence-fiber union, including at face intersections.  The fixed-error certificate shows why an honest set must be allowed to retain locally indistinguishable faces there: exact uniform validity survives, but uniform contraction to the exact optimizer correspondence at any vanishing rate does not.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: In the categorical-instrument model with \(K\geq3\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{face}}\), and indeed any data-based random closed set, cannot simultaneously have asymptotic containment coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly along all \(n^{-1/2}\)-local sequences through intersections of optimal faces and contract in support-function or Hausdorff distance to \(Q_x^*(p_x)\) at any deterministic rate tending to zero.  More precisely, there is an admissible full-compliance local sequence through a codimension-one optimal-face intersection on which either distance is at least \(\sqrt{2}\) with probability bounded away from zero.  Hence neither uniform consistency nor uniform root-\(n\) contraction is possible without selecting a population face.  Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains valid, but any uniform vanishing-rate contraction requires excluding such intersections by a face-separation condition or weakening the target to a local outer limit.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing proof establishes a fixed \(\sqrt{2}\) Hausdorff and support-function error with probability bounded away from zero along \(\tau_n=c/\sqrt n\).  For every deterministic vanishing rate \(r_n\), this implies non-tightness of the error divided by \(r_n\), and it also rules out uniform consistency.  The proposal records that exact consequence while preserving the model class, honesty premise, and local submodel.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Carry the directed claim text and declare the response-fiber, action-mean projection, and support conditions used explicitly by the complete proof spine.

prose_updates.tldr: For the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, the paper identifies the full joint action-mean polytope and solves the resulting randomized minimax-regret game. Its inferential conclusion is a sharp regular--irregular dichotomy: on separated nondegenerate unique faces, the moving-coefficient KKT map is Hadamard differentiable and admits a uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian law; at intersections of optimal faces, no uniformly honest random closed set can contract to the exact optimizer correspondence at any vanishing rate, so uniform consistency itself fails there. The exact Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber union remains uniformly valid at those intersections, but it is deliberately noncontracting there. Pure-rule certificates, the spike-state specialization, the exact three-action joint-versus-rectangle witness, and deployed-regret certification complete the decision analysis.

project_justification.gap: Song et al.'s model M1 supplies the compatible response-law restrictions for discrete instruments and outcomes, but it does not provide randomized minimax-regret optimization or sampling inference for the resulting optimizer correspondence. Existing random-linear-program theory generally fixes constraint normals, while here the observable multinomial table changes both the feasible response bases and the active regret coefficients. The unresolved inferential issue was therefore not merely differentiability on a regular face, but whether any uniformly honest contraction can survive intersections of optimal faces.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies the binary-outcome, finite-covariate-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s M1 and links response-type partial identification to a finite randomized saddle program. It separates regular laws, where observable basis, slack, reduced-cost, and active-face margins stabilize the KKT system and yield root-\(n\) Gaussian inference, from irregular face intersections, where locally indistinguishable laws force a fixed optimizer-set error and preclude contraction at every vanishing rate.
project_justification.fill: The positive result gives the explicit moving-coefficient derivative and uniform Gaussian policy-and-value law on separated nondegenerate unique faces. The negative result gives an explicit full-compliance local submodel proving that no data-based random closed set can combine uniform asymptotic coverage with contraction at any vanishing rate at face intersections; in particular, neither uniform consistency nor uniform root-\(n\) contraction is possible. Exact finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage is the valid noncontracting fallback. The rectangle-safety counterexample also applies to Hruza et al.'s broader overlapping bound-agnostic class by inclusion, but the positive sampling and KKT theorem is proved only for this paper's narrower response-type model and does not transfer by that inclusion.

prose_updates.related_work: Manski2000TreatmentChoice separates treatment choice from point identification, and Stoye2007ManyTreatments supplies the spike-state population allocation benchmark recovered here when every spike is feasible. Masten2023ManyTreatmentRules and MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Asymptotics analyze different repeated-sample or local-Gaussian treatment-choice problems, whereas this paper studies fixed-law inference for a population mixed-action optimizer under partial identification. Cui2021PartialIDDecisions randomizes a binary action from marginal contrast bounds; it does not optimize three or more actions against a joint categorical-instrument response polytope. SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies model M1's response-law compatibility restrictions; the present model is its binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization, not a claim about all of models M1--M5. SachsEtAl2023SymbolicBounds and MastinJailletChin2014RandomizedRegret provide the response-function linear-program and finite saddle ingredients, whose composition is treated as background. HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL studies a broader, overlapping bound-agnostic class and a coordinatewise-interval decision rule. Inclusion carries the paper's negative rectangle-safety witness to that broader class, but it does not carry the positive response-basis, KKT, or Gaussian theorem. BonnansShapiro2000Perturbation informs the separated-face analysis; KlattMunkZemel2022RandomLP and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence concern fixed-coefficient formulations that do not cover the moving active normals here. FangSantos2019DirectionalInference motivates derivative-aware inference at nonsmooth maps, while the theorem here proves the stronger obstruction that a uniformly honest random closed set cannot contract at any vanishing rate to the exact optimizer set at face intersections, and hence cannot be uniformly consistent there. ClopperPearson1934Binomial and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007Sets inform the exact, noncontracting confidence-fiber fallback.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian policy-and-regret law is restricted to the observable nondegenerate unique-face class with fixed-support, response-basis, rank, slack, reduced-cost, and active-weight margins. At face intersections, the impossibility theorem rules out every uniformly honest vanishing-rate contraction to the exact optimizer correspondence, including uniform consistency and uniform root-\(n\) contraction; the Bonferroni confidence-fiber union remains valid but can be conservative and noncontracting. The negative rectangle-safety witness transfers to broader classes containing the displayed law, including the overlapping Hruza et al. class, but the positive active-basis and KKT theory requires this paper's response-type structure and stated margins.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The maintained causal model is the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, with finite randomized instrument support, categorical treatment, response-type exogeneity, consistency, exclusion, positive stratum--instrument support, and response-fiber compatibility. The response-function projection and its composition with a finite randomized-regret linear program are background ingredients. Uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian inference is proved only on the separated nondegenerate unique-face class; it is not claimed at face intersections. At those intersections, an explicit full-compliance local submodel proves that every uniformly honest random closed set must forgo contraction at every vanishing rate to the exact optimizer correspondence, so even uniform consistency is impossible unless a population face is selected or the target is weakened to a local outer limit. The exact Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber set remains finite-sample valid without a contraction claim. Hruza et al.'s class is broader and overlapping rather than identical: only the negative rectangle-safety counterexample transfers upward by inclusion, while the positive sampling and KKT theorem does not.
